I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best and it fits my well irrigation. I have farmed for a long time, my household is small, and some labor is away off-farm, so I will not make this year complicated. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.4 mu for cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen to support a steady stand, and give a few irrigations because water from the well is available and wheat in my area responds well to it. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield and more stable ears, and I will fertilize a bit heavier than wheat, but I will keep irrigation moderate because summer rain can help. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it takes more care and picking labor, but I will still plant it since I already grow it and it spreads my risk. I will manage all three crops in a practical way, with moderate fertilizer, a limited number of pesticide sprays, and simple tillage that matches the labor I have.
